claim: The congression of chromosomes to the spindle equator involves the directed motility of bi-orientated sister kinetochores.
source: The congression of chromosomes to the spindle equator involves the directed motility of bi-orientated sister kinetochores.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that represents established knowledge about chromosome congression.

claim: Sister kinetochores bind bundles of dynamic microtubules.
source: Sister kinetochores bind bundles of dynamic microtubules and are physically connected through centromeric chromatin.
evidence: This is established knowledge about kinetochore structure and function.

claim: Sister kinetochores are physically connected through centromeric chromatin.
source: Sister kinetochores bind bundles of dynamic microtubules and are physically connected through centromeric chromatin.
evidence: This is established knowledge about kinetochore structure.

claim: Switching is initiated by both the leading (microtubules depolymerising) or trailing (microtubules polymerising) kinetochore.
source: We discover that switching is initiated by both the leading (microtubules depolymerising) or trailing (microtubules polymerising) kinetochore.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on analysis of thousands of switching events.

claim: Trail-driven switching generates an overstretch of the chromatin that relaxes over the following half-period.
source: Surprisingly, trail-driven switching generates an overstretch of the chromatin that relaxes over the following half-period.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study based on analysis of inter-sister distance dynamics.

claim: The overstretch observation rules out the involvement of a tension sensor, the central premise of the long-standing tension-model.
source: This rules out the involvement of a tension sensor, the central premise of the long-standing tension-model.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed overstretch data that contradicts the tension model.

claim: Clocks set the intrinsic-switching time of the two kinetochore-attached microtubule fibres.
source: Instead, our data support a model in which clocks set the intrinsic-switching time of the two kinetochore-attached microtubule fibres, with the centromeric spring tension operating as a feedback to slow or accelerate the clocks.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the data showing invariant run times regardless of preceding event type.

claim: The centromeric spring tension operates as a feedback to slow or accelerate the clocks.
source: Instead, our data support a model in which clocks set the intrinsic-switching time of the two kinetochore-attached microtubule fibres, with the centromeric spring tension operating as a feedback to slow or accelerate the clocks.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the observed relationship between tension and switching dynamics.

claim: Bi-orientation begins immediately after nuclear envelope breakdown during prometaphase.
source: Bi-orientation begins immediately after nuclear envelope breakdown during prometaphase when scattered chromosomes engage the nascent mitotic spindle, and concludes with the formation of the metaphase plate – a state where all sister kinetochores are bi-orientated and aligned on the equator of a bipolar spindle (McIntosh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to McIntosh et al., 2012.

claim: Bi-orientation concludes with the formation of the metaphase plate where all sister kinetochores are bi-orientated and aligned on the equator of a bipolar spindle.
source: Bi-orientation begins immediately after nuclear envelope breakdown during prometaphase when scattered chromosomes engage the nascent mitotic spindle, and concludes with the formation of the metaphase plate – a state where all sister kinetochores are bi-orientated and aligned on the equator of a bipolar spindle (McIntosh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to McIntosh et al., 2012.

claim: The kinetochore-fibre (K-fibre) is typically 20–25 microtubules in human cells.
source: These two movement states reflect the balance of microtubule polymerisation/depolymerisation within the kinetochore-fibre (K-fibre), which is typically 20–25 microtubules in human cells (Compton, 2000; Rieder, 2005; Wendell et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Compton, 2000; Rieder, 2005; Wendell et al., 1993.

claim: K-fibres are rarely coherent.
source: While such K-fibres are rarely coherent, there is a small polymerisation bias between sister kinetochores (Armond et al., 2015; VandenBeldt et al., 2006) and they can be thought of as being in either a net polymerising or depolymerising state.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Armond et al., 2015; VandenBeldt et al., 2006.

claim: There is a small polymerisation bias between sister kinetochores.
source: While such K-fibres are rarely coherent, there is a small polymerisation bias between sister kinetochores (Armond et al., 2015; VandenBeldt et al., 2006) and they can be thought of as being in either a net polymerising or depolymerising state.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Armond et al., 2015; VandenBeldt et al., 2006.

claim: Kinetochores undergo periods of relatively constant velocity separated by abrupt changes in direction, termed 'directional instability'.
source: Kinetochores were shown to undergo periods of relatively constant velocity separated by abrupt changes in direction – a behaviour termed 'directional instability'.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies in newt lung cells using video-enhanced differential interference contrast microscopy.

claim: Weakening the centromeric chromatin with a laser uncoupled the normally coordinated motility of sister kinetochores.
source: Subsequent experiments demonstrated that weakening the centromeric chromatin which links the sisters (with a laser) uncoupled the normally coordinated motility of sister kinetochores (Skibbens et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Skibbens et al., 1995.

claim: In the tension model, tension in the centromeric chromatin triggers a lead sister switch (P-to-AP) at a certain threshold.
source: These experiments led to a model (also see Rieder and Salmon, 1994) in which tension in the centromeric chromatin triggers a lead sister switch (P-to-AP) at a certain threshold, the loss of tension then triggering a directional switch in the second sister (AP-to-P).
evidence: This describes the standard tension model supported by citations.

claim: In the tension model, the loss of tension triggers a directional switch in the second sister (AP-to-P).
source: These experiments led to a model (also see Rieder and Salmon, 1994) in which tension in the centromeric chromatin triggers a lead sister switch (P-to-AP) at a certain threshold, the loss of tension then triggering a directional switch in the second sister (AP-to-P).
evidence: This describes the standard tension model supported by citations.

claim: Recent kinetochore-tracking experiments in PtK1 cells show that switching initiates at maximum inter-kinetochore stretch.
source: More recent kinetochore-tracking experiments in PtK1 cells are consistent with this model and show that switching initiates at maximum inter-kinetochore stretch (Wan et al., 2012), schematic shown in Figure 1.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Wan et al., 2012 and reference to Figure 1.

claim: The polar ejection force increases with proximity to the pole and pushes chromosomes towards the metaphase plate.
source: The polar ejection force, which increases with proximity to the pole, pushes the chromosomes towards the metaphase plate.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the polar ejection force.

claim: When chromosomes stray far from the equator, the anti-poleward force increases the load on the leading (P) kinetochore and promotes switching.
source: When chromosomes stray far from the equator, this anti-poleward force increases the load on the leading (P) kinetochore and promotes switching – an idea supported by experiments in newt and human cells (Ke et al., 2009; Stumpff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experiments in Ke et al., 2009; Stumpff et al., 2012.

claim: The standard tension model predicts a fixed sequence of sister kinetochore-switching events during a directional reversal – lead switch first, followed by trail.
source: The standard tension model thus predicts a fixed sequence of sister kinetochore-switching events during a directional reversal – lead switch first, followed by trail.
evidence: This is an inference about what the standard tension model predicts.

claim: Existing kinetochore-tracking assays have a frame rate in the 7.5–15 s range.
source: Existing kinetochore-tracking assays have a frame rate in the 7.5–15 s range (Dumont et al., 2012; Jaqaman et al., 2010; Wan et al., 2012), meaning that detailed analysis of the switching mechanism has not been possible to date.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Dumont et al., 2012; Jaqaman et al., 2010; Wan et al., 2012.

claim: The frame rate of existing kinetochore-tracking assays means that detailed analysis of the switching mechanism has not been possible to date.
source: Existing kinetochore-tracking assays have a frame rate in the 7.5–15 s range (Dumont et al., 2012; Jaqaman et al., 2010; Wan et al., 2012), meaning that detailed analysis of the switching mechanism has not been possible to date.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal resolution limitations of existing assays.

claim: The study used spinning disk confocal microscopy to capture 3D image stacks every 2 s over 150 time steps.
source: To improve resolution, we used spinning disk confocal microscopy to capture 3D image stacks every 2 s over 150 time steps in HeLa-K cells expressing a marker for the kinetochores (either eGFP-CENP-A or eGFP-CENP-A eGFP-Centrin1; Figure 2B; Video 1, Video 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Phototoxicity was minimal, as >90% of cells successfully underwent anaphase.
source: Phototoxicity was minimal, as >90% of cells successfully underwent anaphase.
evidence: This is a data-based observation from the study.

claim: The study implemented 3D Gaussian mixture model fitting for determining sub-pixel spot locations.
source: Sister kinetochores were tracked as previously described (Jaqaman et al., 2010), except that we implemented 3D Gaussian mixture model fitting for determining sub-pixel spot locations (Thomann et al., 2002 see Figure 2A, C; Videos 3–5) – important here because our faster time sampling results in a smaller inter-frame spot displacement requiring higher localisation accuracy.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, with citation to Thomann et al., 2002.

claim: The sub-pixel tracking gives high theoretical positional accuracy (x,y = ± 2.8 nm; z = ± 5.7 nm).
source: This sub-pixel (super-resolution) tracking gives high theoretical positional accuracy (x,y = ± 2.8 nm; z = ± 5.7 nm; see 'Materials and methods') and reveals kinetochore dynamics in exquisite detail (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a calculated theoretical accuracy based on the methodology.

claim: Sister kinetochores had a mean inter-kinetochore distance of ~910 nm.
source: Consistent with previous work (Jaqaman et al., 2010; Vladimirou et al., 2013), sister kinetochores had a mean inter-kinetochore distance of ~910 nm and underwent quasi-periodic oscillations normal to the metaphase plate with a half-period of 35 s (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a data-based observation from the study, consistent with previous work cited.

claim: Sister kinetochores underwent quasi-periodic oscillations normal to the metaphase plate with a half-period of 35 s.
source: Consistent with previous work (Jaqaman et al., 2010; Vladimirou et al., 2013), sister kinetochores had a mean inter-kinetochore distance of ~910 nm and underwent quasi-periodic oscillations normal to the metaphase plate with a half-period of 35 s (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a data-based observation from the study, consistent with previous work cited.

claim: The Bayesian switching point inference algorithm has an accuracy of 94% on simulated data.
source: We tested this algorithm on simulated data where the true switch time is known giving accuracies of 94% (see 'Materials and methods'; Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a data-based validation of the algorithm on simulated data.

claim: The study identified switch events in the trajectories of 1529 sister pairs across 55 eGFP-CENP-A cells.
source: Next, we identified switch events in the trajectories of 1529 sister pairs across 55 eGFP-CENP-A cells and calculated the frequency that lead or trailing sisters switch first (n=9022 events ending a coherent run).
evidence: This describes the dataset analyzed in the study.

claim: The study analyzed 9022 events ending a coherent run.
source: Next, we identified switch events in the trajectories of 1529 sister pairs across 55 eGFP-CENP-A cells and calculated the frequency that lead or trailing sisters switch first (n=9022 events ending a coherent run).
evidence: This describes the dataset analyzed in the study.

claim: The fraction of LIDS and TIDS are 54.3% and 34.8%, respectively.
source: These criteria illustrate that there is a strong lead bias with the fraction of LIDS and TIDS being 54.3% and 34.8%, respectively, the remaining fraction (10.9%) of events being joint.

claim: 10.9% of events are joint directional switches (JDS).
source: These criteria illustrate that there is a strong lead bias with the fraction of LIDS and TIDS being 54.3% and 34.8%, respectively, the remaining fraction (10.9%) of events being joint.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: There is a strong lead bias with a lead-to-trail bias of 1.56:1.
source: These data demonstrate that trailing sister switching is suppressed in human cells, leaving a lead-to-trail bias of 1.56:1.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: Trailing sister switching is suppressed in human cells.
source: These data demonstrate that trailing sister switching is suppressed in human cells, leaving a lead-to-trail bias of 1.56:1.

claim: Current directional switching models propose that switching of the lead kinetochore is initiated when the inter-sister distance reaches a maximum stretch.
source: Current directional switching models propose that switching of the lead kinetochore is initiated when the inter-sister distance (centromere spring) reaches a maximum stretch (tension) (Rieder and Salmon, 1994; Skibbens et al., 1995; Skibbens et al., 1993; Wan et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the current model supported by multiple citations.

claim: No mechanism has been proposed to explain trail first switching.
source: Moreover, no mechanism has been proposed to explain trail first switching; trailing sister initiated switching has also been reported for PtK1 cells at a 15% frequency (Dumont et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Trailing sister initiated switching has been reported for PtK1 cells at a 15% frequency.
source: Moreover, no mechanism has been proposed to explain trail first switching; trailing sister initiated switching has also been reported for PtK1 cells at a 15% frequency (Dumont et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Dumont et al., 2012.

claim: LIDS and TIDS both have strong pre-event and post-event inter-sister distance signatures.
source: By aligning profiles of the inter-sister distance – which reflects tension in the centromeric chromatin, 40 s before and 40 s after the first sister switching event (Figure 4A), we demonstrate clearly that LIDS and TIDS both have strong pre-event and post-event inter-sister distance signatures (Figure 4A; compare red [TIDS] and black [LIDS] traces).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance increases corresponding to an average increase of spring stretch from 14% to 20% over the 20 s prior to the first sister switch.
source: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance increases corresponding to an average increase of spring stretch from 14% to 20% over the 20 s prior to the first sister switch, stabilises 4 s prior to that switch event and then decreases rapidly during the 6 s following the first sister switch to a minimum average stretch of 5% (Figure 4A; black trace).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance stabilises 4 s prior to the switch event.
source: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance increases corresponding to an average increase of spring stretch from 14% to 20% over the 20 s prior to the first sister switch, stabilises 4 s prior to that switch event and then decreases rapidly during the 6 s following the first sister switch to a minimum average stretch of 5% (Figure 4A; black trace).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance decreases rapidly during the 6 s following the first sister switch to a minimum average stretch of 5%.
source: For a LIDS, the inter-sister distance increases corresponding to an average increase of spring stretch from 14% to 20% over the 20 s prior to the first sister switch, stabilises 4 s prior to that switch event and then decreases rapidly during the 6 s following the first sister switch to a minimum average stretch of 5% (Figure 4A; black trace).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A baseline rest length of 788 nm was determined from nocodazole-treated cells.
source: Here, we used a baseline rest length of 788 nm determined from nocodazole-treated cells (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the experimental determination of the baseline rest length.

claim: The LIDS event leaves the two K-fibres in a polymerising state, which decreases the inter-sister distance.
source: The LIDS event leaves the two K-fibres in a polymerising state, which decreases the inter-sister distance; this is in line with the standard model where the inter-sister distance will then undergo extension over the following coherent run (Figure 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed dynamics and the standard model.

claim: The relaxation of the spring immediately prior to the first sister switch appears to be the result of the lead sister slowing down.
source: The relaxation of the spring immediately prior to the first sister switch appears to be the result of the lead sister slowing down (data not shown).
evidence: This is an inference based on data analysis.

claim: The velocity slows at maximal inter-sister stretch in Ptk1 cells.
source: This would be in line with experiments in Ptk1 cells in which the velocity slows at maximal inter-sister stretch (Wan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Wan et al., 2012.

claim: The switching of the second (trailing) sister correlates with the reduction in spring extension to near zero.
source: Finally, the switching of the second (trailing) sister correlates with the reduction in spring extension to near zero (Figure 4A), possibly suggesting that switching is the result of a loss of tension in accord with the standard tension model (Rieder et al., 1994).
evidence: This is a data-based observation with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: For a TIDS, the inter-sister distance is much lower prior to the first sister switch.
source: However, the profile for a TIDS is distinct: the inter-sister distance is much lower prior to the first sister switch (Figure 4A; red trace).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For a TIDS, the maximum stretch (25%) is only reached 4 s after the switch has occurred.
source: The maximum stretch (25%) is only reached 4 s after the switch has occurred.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: The TIDS itself is necessary to build up tension in the centromeric chromatin.
source: This indicates that the TIDS itself is necessary to build up tension in the centromeric chromatin while the maximum inter-sister stretch is higher than that seen during LIDS (average 200 nm spring extension).
evidence: This is an inference from the observed dynamics of TIDS.

claim: The maximum inter-sister stretch during TIDS is higher than that seen during LIDS (average 200 nm spring extension).
source: This indicates that the TIDS itself is necessary to build up tension in the centromeric chromatin while the maximum inter-sister stretch is higher than that seen during LIDS (average 200 nm spring extension).

claim: Following a TIDS event, the centromeric spring tension escalates during the directional switch and starts to relax 4 s after the directional switch.
source: However, following a TIDS event, the centromeric spring tension escalates during the directional switch and starts to relax 4 s after the directional switch (Figure 4A), suggesting that the tension remains high over the following run.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For runs with a preceding LIDS, the inter-sister distance rose over the following run.
source: For runs with a preceding switch that was either a LIDS or a TIDS, the inter-sister distance rose (Figure 4C) or relaxed (Figure 4D) over the following run, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For runs with a preceding TIDS, the inter-sister distance relaxed over the following run.
source: For runs with a preceding switch that was either a LIDS or a TIDS, the inter-sister distance rose (Figure 4C) or relaxed (Figure 4D) over the following run, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: For runs starting after a TIDS, the subsequent directional switch still has a LIDS bias (1.53 compared to a bias of 1.64 for a preceding LIDS).
source: Crucially, for runs starting after a TIDS the subsequent directional switch still has a LIDS bias (1.53 compared to a bias of 1.64 for a preceding LIDS), while the (median) time of the coherent run is identical to that following a LIDS (27.1 ± 0.21 s for TIDS, 26.7 ± 0.29 s for LIDS, p=5.5%).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: The median time of the coherent run is identical following a TIDS or LIDS (27.1 ± 0.21 s for TIDS, 26.7 ± 0.29 s for LIDS, p=5.5%).
source: Crucially, for runs starting after a TIDS the subsequent directional switch still has a LIDS bias (1.53 compared to a bias of 1.64 for a preceding LIDS), while the (median) time of the coherent run is identical to that following a LIDS (27.1 ± 0.21 s for TIDS, 26.7 ± 0.29 s for LIDS, p=5.5%).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: TIDS take a shorter amount of time to complete (second sister switches) than LIDS, median times 4.05 ± 0.15 s versus 4.31 ± 0.13 s, respectively (p=1.3 x 10–4).
source: However, TIDS take a shorter amount of time to complete (second sister switches) than LIDS, median times 4.05 ± 0.15 s versus 4.31 ± 0.13 s, respectively (p=1.3 x 10–4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: Kinetochore oscillations are robust to sister switching order.
source: In essence, kinetochore oscillations are robust to sister switching order and the dynamics of the kinetochores is nearly identical after a TIDS and LIDS, except that the inter-sister distance decreases instead of increases, respectively (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is an inference from the data analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: The dynamics of the kinetochores is nearly identical after a TIDS and LIDS, except that the inter-sister distance decreases instead of increases, respectively.
source: In essence, kinetochore oscillations are robust to sister switching order and the dynamics of the kinetochores is nearly identical after a TIDS and LIDS, except that the inter-sister distance decreases instead of increases, respectively (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Under a LIDS, the inter-sister distance relaxes then increases over the subsequent coherent run.
source: Our observations suggest that the classic choreography (Figure 1) represents half of the dynamic with the inter-sister distance relaxing under a LIDS then increasing over the subsequent coherent run – depolymerising K-fibres pulling kinetochores with greater force than polymerising fibres push.
evidence: This is an inference from the data analysis.

claim: Depolymerising K-fibres pull kinetochores with greater force than polymerising fibres push.
source: Our observations suggest that the classic choreography (Figure 1) represents half of the dynamic with the inter-sister distance relaxing under a LIDS then increasing over the subsequent coherent run – depolymerising K-fibres pulling kinetochores with greater force than polymerising fibres push.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed dynamics.

claim: Under a TIDS, the inter-sister distance is overstretched and relaxes during the subsequent coherent run.
source: However, under a TIDS the inter-sister distance is overstretched and relaxes during the subsequent coherent run – the centromeric spring force increasing the velocity of the trailing sister so that it exceeds that of the lead sister.

claim: Under a TIDS, the centromeric spring force increases the velocity of the trailing sister so that it exceeds that of the lead sister.

claim: Directional switching cannot be triggered by a threshold on the spring tension.
source: This TIDS choreography implies that directional switching cannot be triggered by a threshold on the spring tension as overstretching and subsequent relaxation of the spring tension prior to a directional switch are a natural part of metaphase kinetochore oscillations.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed TIDS dynamics that contradicts the tension threshold model.

claim: Overstretching and subsequent relaxation of the spring tension prior to a directional switch are a natural part of metaphase kinetochore oscillations.
source: This TIDS choreography implies that directional switching cannot be triggered by a threshold on the spring tension as overstretching and subsequent relaxation of the spring tension prior to a directional switch are a natural part of metaphase kinetochore oscillations.

claim: Kinetochores move in 3D with the kinetochore sister axis being compliant to twist away from the metaphase plate normal.
source: Kinetochores move in 3D with the kinetochore sister axis being compliant to twist away from the metaphase plate normal (Figure 2D,E).

claim: The twist and inter-sister distance are inversely correlated (r=–0.13, significant at p<10–200).
source: The twist and inter-sister distance are in fact inversely correlated (r=–0.13, significant at p<10–200), with twist showing inverted profiles over switching events relative to that for the inter-sister distance (Figure 5).

claim: Twist shows inverted profiles over switching events relative to that for the inter-sister distance.

claim: For a LIDS, the twist of the sisters falls prior to the switch and increases after the switch event.

claim: For a TIDS, the twist of the sisters increases prior to the switch and decreases after the switch event.

claim: A high inter-sister stretch, indicative of a high inter-sister tension, aligns the sisters, reducing the twist.

claim: A low stretch, with low tension, allows the twist angle to increase under thermal and mechanical fluctuations.

claim: The kinetochore can inhibit catastrophe when under tension, as shown by biophysical experiments using purified budding yeast kinetochores.
source: This may reflect the ability of the kinetochore to inhibit catastrophe when under tension – as shown by biophysical experiments using purified budding yeast kinetochores (Akiyoshi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Akiyoshi et al., 2010.

claim: If tension falls too low (or fails to build up), a TIDS occurs (as microtubules in the K-fibre undergo catastrophe).
source: If that tension falls too low (or fails to build up), a TIDS occurs (as microtubules in the K-fibre undergo catastrophe; Figure 6).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the data and shown in Figure 6.

claim: During a LIDS, the second sister (previously trailing) switches under the loss of the tension in the centromeric chromatin.
source: The same stabilisation mechanism can be invoked to explain switching resolution – during a LIDS the second sister (previously trailing), switches under the loss of the tension in the centromeric chromatin.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the data.

claim: When tension remains high enough to stabilise the trailing sister, then the lead sister switches because of its clock.
source: When tension remains high enough to stabilise the trailing sister, then the lead sister switches because of its clock.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the data.

claim: The escalating force during a TIDS (after the trailing sister switches) could accelerate the lead sister clock triggering switching of the second sister.
source: The escalating force during a TIDS (after the trailing sister switches) could accelerate the lead sister clock triggering switching of the second sister.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The rescue rate of in vitro microtubules attached to kinetochores increases under tension.
source: Again, this reflects the increase in the rescue rate of in vitro microtubules attached to kinetochores as shown in Akiyoshi et al., 2010, while it emphasises that the two sisters are not symmetrical and the time since their last switch event determines which sister switches.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Akiyoshi et al., 2010.

claim: The two sisters are not symmetrical and the time since their last switch event determines which sister switches.
source: Again, this reflects the increase in the rescue rate of in vitro microtubules attached to kinetochores as shown in Akiyoshi et al., 2010, while it emphasises that the two sisters are not symmetrical and the time since their last switch event determines which sister switches.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed dynamics.

claim: Kinetochores display a range of stochasticity in their trajectories, from near deterministic oscillations to the near random.
source: First, kinetochores are known to display a range of stochasticity in their trajectories, from near deterministic oscillations to the near random (Jaqaman et al., 2010; Magidson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Jaqaman et al., 2010; Magidson et al., 2011.

claim: The duration of a coherent run has a large variability with a coefficient of variation of 0.45.
source: Second, the switching times are stochastic; the duration of a coherent run has a large variability with a coefficient of variation (standard deviation [SD]/mean) of 0.45, similar for both runs terminated by an LIDS (mean time and SD 29.6 ± 12.7 s) or a TIDS (29.2 ± 13.6 s, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Runs terminated by an LIDS have a mean time and SD of 29.6 ± 12.7 s.
source: Second, the switching times are stochastic; the duration of a coherent run has a large variability with a coefficient of variation (standard deviation [SD]/mean) of 0.45, similar for both runs terminated by an LIDS (mean time and SD 29.6 ± 12.7 s) or a TIDS (29.2 ± 13.6 s, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Runs terminated by a TIDS have a mean time and SD of 29.2 ± 13.6 s.
source: Second, the switching times are stochastic; the duration of a coherent run has a large variability with a coefficient of variation (standard deviation [SD]/mean) of 0.45, similar for both runs terminated by an LIDS (mean time and SD 29.6 ± 12.7 s) or a TIDS (29.2 ± 13.6 s, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The clock mechanism is inherently stochastic.
source: Thus, although we have invoked a clock mechanism as a switching time regulator, it is inherently stochastic.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed variability in switching times.

claim: The stochasticity could stem from both the number and depolymerisation/polymerisation state of individual microtubules that make up the K-fibre.
source: This stochasticity could stem from both the number and depolymerisation/polymerisation state of individual microtubules that make up the K-fibre.
evidence: This is speculation about the source of stochasticity.

claim: The fraction of microtubules that are in a polymerising state within a K-fibre is highly variable among kinetochores.
source: The fraction of microtubules that are in a polymerising state within a K-fibre is highly variable among kinetochores (Armond et al., 2015), indicating that growing and shrinking K-fibres are unlikely to be composed of fully coherent microtubules.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Armond et al., 2015.

claim: Growing and shrinking K-fibres are unlikely to be composed of fully coherent microtubules.
source: The fraction of microtubules that are in a polymerising state within a K-fibre is highly variable among kinetochores (Armond et al., 2015), indicating that growing and shrinking K-fibres are unlikely to be composed of fully coherent microtubules.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed variability in microtubule states.

claim: The signatures in Figure 4 are a mean behaviour, while variability in the inter-sister stretch throughout the dynamics is large.
source: Third, the signatures in Figure 4 are a mean behaviour, while variability in the inter-sister stretch throughout the dynamics is in fact large.
evidence: This is an observation about the data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS only show marginal separation before the switching event (–4 s).
source: This can be seen at the population level of trajectories, where the inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS only show marginal separation before the switching event (–4 s), are hardly separated at the event, while separation increases after the event (+4 s) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS are hardly separated at the event.
source: This can be seen at the population level of trajectories, where the inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS only show marginal separation before the switching event (–4 s), are hardly separated at the event, while separation increases after the event (+4 s) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The separation of inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS increases after the event (+4 s).
source: This can be seen at the population level of trajectories, where the inter-sister distance distributions for LIDS and TIDS only show marginal separation before the switching event (–4 s), are hardly separated at the event, while separation increases after the event (+4 s) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The inter-sister distance distribution over a switching event is far from bimodal.
source: The inter-sister distance distribution over a switching event is in fact far from bimodal; a mixture of two Gaussian distributions requires the respective means to be separated by at least 2 SDs to be bimodal, the largest we observe is 70% at 4 s post event (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The signatures shown in Figure 4 are not a universal behaviour but only detectable on averaging.
source: Therefore, we have to conclude that the signatures shown in Figure 4 are not a universal behaviour but only detectable on averaging; that is, the actual switching process is highly stochastic.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed variability in the data.

claim: The actual switching process is highly stochastic.
source: Therefore, we have to conclude that the signatures shown in Figure 4 are not a universal behaviour but only detectable on averaging; that is, the actual switching process is highly stochastic.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed variability in the data.

claim: Directional switching may be a composite process that integrates over multiple signals.
source: It may be that analysis of the most deterministic trajectories will reduce this stochasticity in the switching dynamics and signatures. However, directional switching may be a composite process that integrates over multiple signals, that is, tension may not be the only determinant; the stochasticity in our signatures would then be due to measuring only one of these determinants.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of directional switching.

claim: Tension may not be the only determinant of directional switching.
source: It may be that analysis of the most deterministic trajectories will reduce this stochasticity in the switching dynamics and signatures. However, directional switching may be a composite process that integrates over multiple signals, that is, tension may not be the only determinant; the stochasticity in our signatures would then be due to measuring only one of these determinants.
evidence: This is speculation about the determinants of directional switching.

claim: It remains unknown to what extent the stochasticity in switching time and switching type explains the observed diversity in kinetochore trajectory dynamics.
source: It remains unknown to what extent the stochasticity in switching time and switching type explains the observed diversity in kinetochore trajectory dynamics, or whether other sources of variability exist.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: The leading sister typically initiates directional switching.
source: This paper demonstrates how dynamic and mechanistic insight can be extracted from high-resolution tracking data. Although the leading sister typically initiates directional switching, the reverse switching order is also frequently observed (Figure 3D), with directional switching biases, timings and subsequent oscillations remaining robust to such events.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: The reverse switching order (trail first) is also frequently observed.
source: This paper demonstrates how dynamic and mechanistic insight can be extracted from high-resolution tracking data. Although the leading sister typically initiates directional switching, the reverse switching order is also frequently observed (Figure 3D), with directional switching biases, timings and subsequent oscillations remaining robust to such events.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Directional switching biases, timings and subsequent oscillations remain robust to switching order.
source: This paper demonstrates how dynamic and mechanistic insight can be extracted from high-resolution tracking data. Although the leading sister typically initiates directional switching, the reverse switching order is also frequently observed (Figure 3D), with directional switching biases, timings and subsequent oscillations remaining robust to such events.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data analysis.

claim: Event classification is physical and not due to noisy fluctuations in switching times coming from localisation measurement noise.
source: By classifying switching order events, we were able to demonstrate clear stereotypical behaviour associated with these events, with both prior (potentially causal) and post-event signatures in the inter-sister distance dynamics. This confirms that event classification is physical and not due to noisy fluctuations in switching times coming from localisation measurement noise.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed stereotypical signatures.

claim: The data support a new model of kinetochore oscillations comprising mechanical clocks on both the lead and trailing sister.
source: Our data support a new model of kinetochore oscillations comprising mechanical clocks on both the lead and trailing sister, which likely reflect the time- and force-dependent rescue and catastrophe of the K-fibre microtubules.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the data.

claim: The mechanical clocks likely reflect the time- and force-dependent rescue and catastrophe of the K-fibre microtubules.
source: Our data support a new model of kinetochore oscillations comprising mechanical clocks on both the lead and trailing sister, which likely reflect the time- and force-dependent rescue and catastrophe of the K-fibre microtubules.
evidence: This is speculation about the molecular mechanism of the clocks.

claim: The degree of stretch of the inter-sister centromeric chromatin is a major determinant in orchestrating switching.
source: Our analysis suggests that the degree of stretch of the inter-sister centromeric chromatin is a major determinant in orchestrating this switching; first, a mechanism based on stabilisation of the trailing sister polymerisation state through the centromere tension, effectively slowing the trailing sister clock, and second, a clock on the lead sister that is accelerated under high tension (Figure 6).
evidence: This is an inference from the data analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Centromere tension stabilises the trailing sister polymerisation state, effectively slowing the trailing sister clock.
source: Our analysis suggests that the degree of stretch of the inter-sister centromeric chromatin is a major determinant in orchestrating this switching; first, a mechanism based on stabilisation of the trailing sister polymerisation state through the centromere tension, effectively slowing the trailing sister clock, and second, a clock on the lead sister that is accelerated under high tension (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The clock on the lead sister is accelerated under high tension.
source: Our analysis suggests that the degree of stretch of the inter-sister centromeric chromatin is a major determinant in orchestrating this switching; first, a mechanism based on stabilisation of the trailing sister polymerisation state through the centromere tension, effectively slowing the trailing sister clock, and second, a clock on the lead sister that is accelerated under high tension (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The standard tension model of sister kinetochore switching is only able to explain part of the dynamics.
source: Our data indicate that the standard tension model of sister kinetochore switching (Figure 1) is only able to explain part of the dynamics, while it is incompatible with the overstretch and subsequent relaxation of the inter-sister distance following a TIDS.
evidence: This is an inference from the data that contradicts the standard model.

claim: The standard tension model is incompatible with the overstretch and subsequent relaxation of the inter-sister distance following a TIDS.
source: Our data indicate that the standard tension model of sister kinetochore switching (Figure 1) is only able to explain part of the dynamics, while it is incompatible with the overstretch and subsequent relaxation of the inter-sister distance following a TIDS.
evidence: This is an inference from the data that contradicts the standard model.

claim: Kinetochores utilise multiple sensory and fail-safe mechanisms that ensure high-fidelity chromosome organisation within the spindle, despite high levels of stochasticity.
source: Thus, kinetochores utilise multiple sensory and fail-safe mechanisms that ensure high-fidelity chromosome organisation within the spindle, despite high levels of stochasticity.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed robustness of kinetochore dynamics.

claim: HeLa-K cells stably expressing eGFP-CENP-A were used in the study.
source: HeLa-K cells stably expressing eGFP-CENP-A (Jaqaman et al., 2010) or eGFP-CENP-A/eGFP-Centrin 1 were grown in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (Fisher, UK) containing 10% foetal calf serum (Fisher), 100 µg ml-1 penicillin and 100 µg ml-1 streptomycin maintained in 5% CO2 at 37°C in a humidified incubator.
evidence: This describes the cell lines and culture conditions used in the study.

claim: Cells were treated with 2 µg ml-1 nocodazole for between 16 and 24 hr to depolymerise microtubules to measure the inter-sister distance rest length.
source: To measure the inter-sister distance rest length, cells were treated with 2 µg ml-1 nocodazole (Fisher) for between 16 and 24 hr to depolymerise microtubules.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.
